name: Release - Zapier

# Pushes a new version of the Zapier app. Promoting it to the live version stays a manual
# step in the Zapier developer platform, after a review of the version's changes.
#
#   git tag zapier-v0.1.0 && git push origin zapier-v0.1.0
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "zapier-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  push:
    name: zapier push
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: zapier-publish
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: zapier
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - name: Check the tag matches package.json
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/zapier-v}"
          pkg="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          [ "$tag" = "$pkg" ] || { echo "::error::tag zapier-v$tag does not match $pkg"; exit 1; }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - name: Link the app (.zapierapprc from the ZAPIER_APP_ID secret)
        run: |
          [ -n "$ZAPIER_APP_ID" ] || { echo "::error::ZAPIER_APP_ID secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          printf '{"id": %s}\n' "$ZAPIER_APP_ID" > .zapierapprc
        env:
          ZAPIER_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.ZAPIER_APP_ID }}
      - name: Push
        run: npx zapier-platform push
        env:
          ZAPIER_DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAPIER_DEPLOY_KEY }}

name: CI

# Two integrations, one contract (DESIGN.md). Each has its own job so a failure names it.
# Node 22 and 24: n8n 2.x runs on 24, Zapier runs apps on 22, and both CLIs need 22 or later.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  n8n:
    name: n8n (Node ${{ matrix.node }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: n8n
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22", "24"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: n8n/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - name: n8n community-node lint (no errors, no warnings)
        run: npm run lint
      - run: npm test
      - name: No runtime dependencies
        run: node -e 'const d=require("./package.json").dependencies||{}; if(Object.keys(d).length){console.error("runtime dependencies:",d);process.exit(1)}'
      - name: Every node and credential the package declares was built
        run: node -e 'const p=require("./package.json").n8n; for (const f of [...p.nodes,...p.credentials]) require("fs").statSync(f)'

  zapier:
    name: Zapier (Node ${{ matrix.node }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: zapier
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22", "24"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: zapier/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - name: Schema validation
        run: npx zapier-platform validate --without-style

# Writ for Zapier

The [Writ](https://usewrit.app) app for Zapier: scrape and map pages, crawl sites, run the APIs
you built in Writ, watch pages for changes, and start Zaps from Writ events.

## Triggers

| Trigger | Starts a Zap when |
|---|---|
| New Change Detected | a Writ monitor detects that a page changed |
| Workflow Run Finished | a run of a workflow finishes (filter by workflow and outcome) |
| Crawl Finished | a crawl finishes, or fails |
| Monitor Status Changed | a monitor goes down, stops reporting, or recovers |

Triggers are instant: Writ pushes each event to Zapier, signed with a secret made for the
subscription, and the app refuses anything that is not signed with it. Turning the Zap off
removes the subscription in Writ. A change detected again later starts the Zap again.

## Actions

Scrape Page, Map Site, Start Crawl, Run Workflow (waits up to 20 seconds for the result),
Create Monitor, Check Monitor Now.

## Searches

Find Workflow, Find Monitor, Find Records (rows a workflow extracted).

## Connecting

Zapier connects to your Writ account with OAuth. The Writ consent screen lists what Zapier will
be able to do. Disconnecting Zapier in Writ also removes the subscriptions its Zaps made.

Each action uses your Writ account's credits as the same call does from the Writ app or the API.

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm test                      # offline: a stand-in Writ API on localhost
npx zapier-platform validate
```

`test/live.test.js` runs the app against a real Writ server when `WRIT_E2E=1` (the variables
it needs are listed at the top of the file).

name: Release - n8n

# n8n requires community nodes to be published from GitHub Actions with npm provenance.
#
#   git tag n8n-v0.1.0 && git push origin n8n-v0.1.0
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "n8n-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: "Build and verify, but do not publish"
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Publish n8n-nodes-writ
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: npm-publish
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # npm provenance: binds the tarball to this workflow, repo and commit.
      id-token: write
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: n8n
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      # Provenance needs npm >= 9.5; trusted publishing needs >= 11.5.1.
      - name: Use a current npm
        run: npm install -g npm@latest

      - name: Check the tag matches package.json
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/n8n-v}"
          pkg="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          if [ "$tag" != "$pkg" ]; then
            echo "::error::tag n8n-v$tag does not match package.json version $pkg"
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm test

      - name: Verify the tarball
        run: |
          npm pack --dry-run --json > /tmp/pack.json
          node -e '
            const raw = require("/tmp/pack.json");
            const p = Array.isArray(raw) ? raw[0] : Object.values(raw)[0];
            const files = p.files.map(f => f.path);
            for (const want of ["package.json", "README.md", "LICENSE"]) {
              if (!files.includes(want)) { console.error("missing: " + want); process.exit(1); }
            }
            if (!files.some(f => f.startsWith("dist/nodes/"))) { console.error("no dist/nodes"); process.exit(1); }
            if (files.some(f => f.startsWith("test/") || f.endsWith(".ts") && !f.endsWith(".d.ts"))) { console.error("sources in tarball"); process.exit(1); }
          '

      # Authentication: npm trusted publishing (OIDC) from the npm-publish environment.
      # The trusted publisher is allowed to STAGE only: the release waits on npmjs.com until a
      # maintainer approves it with 2FA (Settings of the package, staged versions). A one-time
      # NPM_TOKEN secret on the environment is used instead when present (npm accepts a trusted
      # publisher only for a package that exists, so the very first release needed one).
      # Either way the tarball carries a provenance statement signed by this workflow.
      - name: Stage the release (approve it on npmjs.com)
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.dry_run) }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]; then
            npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "$NPM_TOKEN"
          fi
          npm stage publish --provenance --access public
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          # The package's prepublishOnly (`n8n-node prerelease`) refuses a publish outside
          # `npm run release`; this job already built, linted and tested above.
          RELEASE_MODE: "true"

      - name: Publish dry run
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.dry_run }}
        run: npm stage publish --dry-run --access public
        env:
          RELEASE_MODE: "true"
